data.notes: The report's strongest points are three. It ties "that's an average. What's mine?" to a rewrite of the average-uplift message. It keeps the Adyen results unknown. It rejects the rep's "nothing to do" by pointing to the late analysis and to learning of the split only from the renewal notice. Its main gap is the no-coverage finding: the 9–10 months without a business review is never cited, and the decider insight never concludes that the decision was made before we engaged. Smaller errors: the unverified Brazil/Europe markets are labelled as fact, "I heard from Stripe when I said I was leaving" is hedged instead of used as coverage evidence, and two of Elena's paraphrases (the Adyen test, "approvals") are attributed to Stefan.
